# Breakout Candidates

**Summary.** The breakouts most likely to beat their price in our league come from openings: teammates who left, new starting jobs and year-two or year-three steps, not from skill growth we hope for. Spend in the mid-round on Garland, Buzelis, Brandon Miller, Paul George and Jaren Jackson Jr., add cheap upside bids on Ware, Coward, Edey and Naz Reid, and do not pay market prices for stars whose growth is already priced in. Confirm each case in the first weeks with minutes, free throw attempts and assists, and plan to sell injury-driven roles before the stars come back.

## Breakouts start with an opening

Most busts and breakouts come from injuries and random shooting seasons, not from changes in counting stats. Usage carries over from year to year at 0.83 and minutes at 0.78. So do not bet on a player suddenly getting better. Bet on a role change: an injury, trade or free agency exit that frees up shots. ([08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=436), [08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=534))

When a team loses high-usage players and brings in fewer than it lost, the leftover usage has to go somewhere. Charlotte lost LaMelo Ball and Bridges. Brandon Miller's usage is projected to rise to about 29 or 30 percent, Kon Knueppel's from 22% to about 25%, and Coby White becomes the starting point guard. The Clippers lost Kawhi and Harden, so Darius Garland becomes the main ball handler at about 30% usage. Sacramento lost DeRozan, Westbrook and Schroder, which opens assists for Domantas Sabonis and ball handling for Zach LaVine. ([07-01](https://youtu.be/W3THnI7wWdA?t=855), [Brandon Miller](../profiles/players/brandon-miller.md), [Kon Knueppel](../profiles/players/kon-knueppel.md), [Coby White](../profiles/players/coby-white.md), [Darius Garland](../profiles/players/darius-garland.md), [Domantas Sabonis](../profiles/players/domantas-sabonis.md), [Zach LaVine](../profiles/players/zach-lavine.md))

A player who was third in line next to two stars can jump once one star leaves, mostly in assist rate. Paul George moves from third option to clear second option behind Tatum with Jaylen Brown gone, and his usage is projected at about 26, up from 23. Austin Reaves should get more usage and assists with LeBron gone. Before you bid, check how these players did in games when only one of the stars played. ([07-01](https://youtu.be/W3THnI7wWdA?t=892), [Paul George](../profiles/players/paul-george.md), [Austin Reaves](../profiles/players/austin-reaves.md))

Check the usage picture too. More high-usage stars on a roster means fewer chances, not more. Trae Young gets a big minutes jump, but he shares the ball with Davis and Dybantsa, and experts see a round-3 player. LaMelo Ball's minutes should rise to about 32 in Minnesota while his usage falls next to Edwards. Ty Jerome takes over as starter in Memphis, but his usage is expected to drop from last season. ([07-30](https://youtu.be/TiiaNZCJNs8?t=783), [Trae Young](../profiles/players/trae-young.md), [LaMelo Ball](../profiles/players/lamelo-ball.md), [Ty Jerome](../profiles/players/ty-jerome.md))

## Year two and year three steps

In recent years the big breakouts have moved to year two. Players who did not take a step in year two are the ones who tend to break out in year three. Young players usually get more usage and minutes every year. In our pool, the year-two cases are Cooper Flagg, Cedric Coward, Collin Murray-Boyles and Egor Dëmin. The year-three cases are Matas Buzelis under a new coach and Zach Edey, who may play more than his projected 25 to 28 minutes. ([09-07](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=139), [09-10](https://youtu.be/W-R1dzem32s?t=1602), [08-18](https://youtu.be/FxaSnyk9g90?t=1179), [Cooper Flagg](../profiles/players/cooper-flagg.md), [Cedric Coward](../profiles/players/cedric-coward.md), [Collin Murray-Boyles](../profiles/players/collin-murray-boyles.md), [Egor Dëmin](../profiles/players/egor-demin.md), [Matas Buzelis](../profiles/players/matas-buzelis.md), [Zach Edey](../profiles/players/zach-edey.md))

Big jumps in year four are unlikely for players who showed nothing in their first three seasons. A long-time veteran turning 29 is probably who he is. Brandin Podziemski carries a year-four breakout tag, but his case is really minutes of 30 or more while Butler and Moody are out. Treat him as a 1 to 4 USD minutes bet, not a skill leap. ([09-07](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=157), [07-30](https://youtu.be/TiiaNZCJNs8?t=837), [Brandin Podziemski](../profiles/players/brandin-podziemski.md))

The year-two and year-three rules are a baseline. Judge each player on his own situation. Flagg fits the year-two pattern, but the market already charges for it, so stop at 40 to 45 USD. Ausar Thompson's breakout depends only on extra minutes and assists. One expert does not expect any skill growth. ([08-26](https://youtu.be/sTtFUy7IoJI?t=2034), [Cooper Flagg](../profiles/players/cooper-flagg.md), [Ausar Thompson](../profiles/players/ausar-thompson.md))

## Category signals that confirm it

In category leagues, breakouts come from efficiency at volume, a higher free throw attempt rate and a higher assist rate. This holds for non point guards too. A forward whose assist rate and free throw rate climb over his first six seasons is how a player around 40th overall becomes top 10. ([09-07](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=360), [06-30](https://youtu.be/4GDfg2n2l8o?t=258), [06-28](https://youtu.be/RsjGTgJiKyI?t=1325))

A jump from about 4 to 6.5 or 7 free throw attempts per game can move a player from around 25th to around 5th. FT% is a team ratio, so volume decides how much it matters. Baylor Scheierman's 89% on under one attempt a game barely moves it. Cedric Coward's 84.7% gains value if his shots rise from 10.5 toward 14.2 attempts. ([06-28](https://youtu.be/RsjGTgJiKyI?t=1354), [Baylor Scheierman](../profiles/players/baylor-scheierman.md), [Cedric Coward](../profiles/players/cedric-coward.md))

Small gains add up. A few points better from three, more usage, one more assist and more minutes can lift a player into the top 50. A strong per game rank in limited minutes points to upside if the role grows. Kel'el Ware played 22 minutes and has top 40 upside at 30. Murray-Boyles projects top 70 to 80 at 30 minutes. ([08-12](https://youtu.be/p9XE5jFqhvs?t=2006), [09-21](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=1036), [Kel'el Ware](../profiles/players/kelel-ware.md), [Collin Murray-Boyles](../profiles/players/collin-murray-boyles.md))

Extra volume can also hurt efficiency. Watch whether Miller's 43% FG on 16 to 18 shots falls further. Check that Naz Reid stays at 45% or better on about 13 shots, that Reaves holds near 49%, and that Knueppel holds near 47.5% with more shots. ([Brandon Miller](../profiles/players/brandon-miller.md), [Naz Reid](../profiles/players/naz-reid.md), [Austin Reaves](../profiles/players/austin-reaves.md), [Kon Knueppel](../profiles/players/kon-knueppel.md))

## Where the experts disagree

The notes split on what drives a breakout. One view says breakouts come mostly from injuries and random shooting, not from counting-stat growth, so only the role change matters. The other view says category breakouts show up as a rising free throw rate and assist rate, often in year two or three. For our auction, pay for the opening and treat skill growth as a bonus. Then use free throw attempts and assists in the first weeks to tell which cases are real. ([08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=436), [08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=534), [09-07](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=360), [09-07](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=139))

Experts also split on single players. Knueppel's market rank is in the 30s and 40s, but every expert puts him in the 60s. Ausar Thompson carries a breakout tag, yet one expert expects no skill growth and distrusts the coach's comments about his minutes. Podziemski's year-four tag goes against the note that year-four jumps are rare. In each case, bid at the lower expert price. ([Kon Knueppel](../profiles/players/kon-knueppel.md), [Ausar Thompson](../profiles/players/ausar-thompson.md), [Brandin Podziemski](../profiles/players/brandin-podziemski.md), [09-07](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=157))

## Openings that close

A player's best breakout chance is the season with the most opening. When stars return, expect a step back. Several openings here depend on injuries. Garland, Rui Hachimura and Max Strus gain while Ingram is out. Podziemski and Kristaps Porziņģis gain while Butler is out. Miller gets extra usage while Coby White is out, and Dylan Harper may start while Tobias Harris has a calf strain. ([07-30](https://youtu.be/TiiaNZCJNs8?t=1030), [Darius Garland](../profiles/players/darius-garland.md), [Rui Hachimura](../profiles/players/rui-hachimura.md), [Max Strus](../profiles/players/max-strus.md), [Brandin Podziemski](../profiles/players/brandin-podziemski.md), [Kristaps Porziņģis](../profiles/players/kristaps-porzingis.md), [Brandon Miller](../profiles/players/brandon-miller.md), [Dylan Harper](../profiles/players/dylan-harper.md))

Sell these roles on hot stretches before the star returns, and do it well before the 2027-03-04 trade deadline. Ingram is expected back around Thanksgiving to Christmas. Isaiah Jackson's likely drop point is when Konan Niederhäuser returns around Christmas. ([07-30](https://youtu.be/TiiaNZCJNs8?t=1030), [Brandon Ingram](../profiles/players/brandon-ingram.md), [Isaiah Jackson](../profiles/players/isaiah-jackson.md), [Yanic Konan Niederhäuser](../profiles/players/yanic-konan-niederhauser.md))

## How to bid and what to check

Middle of the auction: pay expert prices for real openings. Garland at about 20 to 25 USD, Buzelis at 15 to 22 USD, Paul George up to 15 to 20 USD, Miller between 20 and 26 USD and Jaren Jackson Jr. in the high teens are the core breakout buys. Do not pay Yahoo prices for Cade Cunningham, or the 44 USD our league paid for Trae Young last season. ([Darius Garland](../profiles/players/darius-garland.md), [Matas Buzelis](../profiles/players/matas-buzelis.md), [Paul George](../profiles/players/paul-george.md), [Brandon Miller](../profiles/players/brandon-miller.md), [Jaren Jackson Jr.](../profiles/players/jaren-jackson.md), [Cade Cunningham](../profiles/players/cade-cunningham.md), [Trae Young](../profiles/players/trae-young.md))

Late in the auction: bid up to about 13 USD for Ware, 10 to 14 USD for Naz Reid, about 11 USD for Edey and 4 to 8 USD for Coward. Use FAB on them once minutes show up, within the 6 adds per week.
